Performers
Sviatoslav Richter (piano), Warsaw National Philharmonic Orchestra (orchestra), Stanisław Wisłocki (conductor) Documented

The Commons filename/description and DG release catalogue agree on all three credits.

[1] [2]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

The performance is of the orchestral concerto, not a two-piano reduction. The exact performing edition and any editorial changes are not specified.

[1]
Recorded
1959 Documented

The file identifies 1959. Youngrok Lee’s DG discography gives 26–⁠28 April 1959 for the concerto; this secondary refinement is not promoted to a precisely verified day for the finale. Commons’ 1 January display is not treated as a session day.

[1] [2] [3]
Place
Warsaw Philharmonic Hall, Warsaw, Poland Inferred, not documented

Two secondary discographies locate the matched Richter/Wisłocki concerto at the Philharmonic Hall. Commons itself does not specify the hall; the connection follows the matching personnel and year.

[2] [3] [1]
Label
Deutsche Grammophon Documented

The selected Commons record names Deutsche Grammophon as source.

[1] [2]
Catalogue
Deutsche Grammophon 138 076 SLPM (stereo LP); corresponding mono issue 18 596 LPM Inferred, not documented

These catalogue numbers belong to the documented matching concerto release. The uploader does not identify the particular LP pressing, CD or other carrier used for the FLAC.

Transfer

The upload does not name a transfer, restoration or mastering engineer. The uploader is not assumed to have performed those tasks.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

1959 is the performance year; the Commons upload date is not a documented date for a transfer or mastering session.

[1]
Processing
Wikimedia Commons supplies an MP3 access derivative of the uploaded FLAC. Documented

The antecedent mastering, editing, equalisation and restoration history is not described. A lossless uploaded container does not prove an unprocessed original source.

[1]
Composition rights
Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies. Inferred, not documented

Rachmaninoff died in 1943. This is a territorial term calculation, not worldwide clearance or a statement about an unidentified modern performing edition.

[6] [7]
Recording rights
Territorial public domain: Commons applies PD-EU-audio to this 1959 recording. Documented

Eligibility rests on the recording-specific PD-EU-audio notice and the documented pre-1963 commercial recording/release, not a composition-only tag. This is territorial: US public-domain status is not established. No worldwide licence or clearance of an unidentified later creative remaster is asserted.
